top_choice_rationale: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a general bond-forming method, confirmed independently for three decades and used daily in synthesis and process chemistry. It needed new ligand classes and a different mechanistic solution from the 2010 C-C couplings. Buchwald and Hartwig independently established the general catalytic reaction, so the two-name allocation and the citation scope are clean, with no strand left uncredited. P001 (targeted protein degradation; Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) is a strong second: the ternary-complex cooperativity argument is chemically persuasive. But a citation on protein degradation will be read as covering the molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray), which the trio omits, no degrader is yet approved, and credit for Sakamoto and Kim is open. Either award is preferable to no award.
